## File and folder naming guidelines

For **source code**, file and folder names must be written in all lower case snake case.

```
// Good names
spi_stm32.c
crc_hw/crc.c

// Bad names
SpiStm32.c
spi-stm32.c
```

## C coding and style guidelines

Most of the styling should be enforced by the clang-format configuration. Consult the configuration
file for guidelines like indentation width, maximum line length, and brace positioning.

The naming convention is as follows

1. Functions, variables, structures, types must use snake case (e.g. `printf()`, `struct linked_list`, `my_type_t`)
2. `typedef` types must have a `_t` postfix (e.g. `typedef struct queue queue_t`)
3. Constants, macros, and enums must be in all capital snake case (e.g. `#define PI (3.1415)`)

Here are some examples

```c
// Good name
bool spi_transmit(...) { ... }

// Bad names
bool SPI_transmit(...) { ... }
bool SpiTransmit(...) { ... }
```

Here are some other guidelines that you must follow

1. Do not `typedef` pointers (i.e. this is bad `typedef struct queue *pqueue_t`)
2. Public functions must be prefixed with its containing module (e.g. `file_open`, `app_init`)
3. Prefer static inline functions over macros
4. Ensure macro constants are wrapped in brackets (i.e. `#define BUFFER_SIZE (128)`)

```c
// Bad name. Searching for public functions related to a module is harder if the function is not
// written with a module prefix
bool is_baro_data_ready() { ... }

// Good name. Your IDE can give you completion for all barometer functions by just typing "baro"
bool baro_is_data_ready() { ... }
```
